status: Future course outline only; production deferred until the six-module Open Systems for AI course is complete
title: Open Cluster Designs for AI
audience: Intermediate designers, integrators and operators who understand the system view from Open Systems for AI
boundary: The main course explains why the domains must agree. This course teaches how to read a documented cluster design and assemble procurement, cabling, facility and operational evidence. Exact packaging and scripts are reserved for the later course intake.

modules.title: Read the Open Cluster Architecture
modules.outcome: Distinguish pod or xPU-node, OPG-M and XOC-N, and locate scale-up, scale-out, storage, front-end and management roles.
teaching: Why repeatable system architectures reduce one-off integration work
Terminology and physical versus logical boundaries
Required workload and deployment assumptions
The architecture document set and its relationship to the wider OCP work
modules.activity: Label an architecture diagram and identify missing workload assumptions.
modules.motion: Build the hierarchy from one node to a pod group and cluster.

modules.title: Read an OPG-M Building Block
modules.outcome: Use the published OPG-128 design to find equipment, topology, cabling and physical requirements.
teaching: The 400G air-cooled reference context
Compute, networking and storage rack roles
Connectivity maps and equipment lists
Adaptation questions for a different deployment
modules.activity: Trace one connection and reconcile it with the equipment kit; record assumptions that cannot be inherited.
modules.motion: Trace one link through a connectivity map without losing its endpoint identity.

modules.title: Compose an XOC-N Cluster
modules.outcome: Explain the cluster-level spine, aggregation and head-end resources that join the pod groups.
teaching: XOC-1k as the published 1,024-xPU example
Composition from eight OPG-128 building blocks
Cluster resource and cabling evidence
Adapting scale while checking shared capacity and management scope
modules.activity: Identify what must be added beyond another pod group when the cluster grows.
modules.motion: Add pod groups, then highlight the cluster resources that must be reviewed.

modules.title: Compare Training and Inference Fabric References
modules.outcome: Choose a reference profile using traffic, tenancy and operational requirements.
teaching: Training traffic and topology choices
Minimal versus Distributed Inference profiles
Gateway and tenant-isolation responsibilities
SONiC and the Hedgehog control plane as documented implementation choices
modules.activity: Select a profile for one training and one inference scenario, with a short justification.
modules.motion: Compare communication patterns without implying measured performance superiority.

modules.title: Assemble Deployment and Operations Evidence
modules.outcome: Connect the architecture kit to installation, facility compatibility and ongoing management.
teaching: Equipment and cable records
Power, cooling, space and service assumptions
Day-0, Day-1 and Day-2 operational evidence in the fabric references
Handoffs among suppliers, facility teams and operators
modules.activity: Assemble a short readiness packet and flag unverified items.
modules.motion: Trace a design assumption into a deployment check and an operational observation.

modules.title: Review a Design and Track the Work Ahead
modules.outcome: Produce a source-linked review and separate published baselines from emerging designs.
teaching: An integrated architecture review exercise
Source version and configuration traceability
The Summit update and liquid-cooled design work in progress
Choosing the next specification or community discussion
modules.activity: Review a small fictional cluster proposal and identify the evidence needed before procurement.
modules.motion: Reveal the review evidence in the same order as the learner decision.

current_work_boundary: The Summit presentation describes a published 400G air-cooled baseline and illustrative 800G/1.6T liquid-cooled work in progress. Recheck contribution status before starting this later course. Do not relabel an in-progress drawing as an approved specification.
assessment: Propose two narrated questions per module plus a source-linked review activity. Detailed scripts and assessment keys will be drafted only during the later course.

cross_references.purpose: Introduce the deployment-oriented next course without expanding this module into a topology lesson.
Provide the shared system-view prerequisite and a concise refresher route.
Delegate detailed facility-specification teaching to the existing live course.

deferred_work: Revalidate all five contribution versions and newer published designs at kickoff.
Complete page-by-page technical and visual analysis before scripts.
Agree total duration and package/SCO architecture separately.
Approve outline, scripts and figure plan before narration, media or SCORM production.
